title: Tenant bailout orchestrator: preemptive short-circuiting and graceful-credit windows for SLO preservation
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds a tenant-level bailout orchestrator that allows preemptive short-circuiting and grace-credit windows to protect cluster-wide SLOs under surge. Rollout gated by feature flag and can be disabled per-tenant. Includes new metrics and dashboards for monitoring bailout activity.
body:
Context and motivation:
We observed multiple incidents where noisy tenants triggered cluster-wide SLO regressions. Existing soft-degradation paths reacted after failure modes (eviction, throttling) had already impacted latency-sensitive tenants. This PR introduces a Tenant Bailout Orchestrator: a preemptive short-circuit + grace-credit system that temporarily redirects high-cost requests for select tenants to a safe fastpath or returns structured fallback responses while keeping global SLOs intact.

What this changes (short):
- New orchestration component (pkg/orchestrator/bailout) that maintains per-tenant 'grace credits' and short-circuit state machines.
- Admission hook in serving runtime to evaluate bailout predicates before expensive KV/cache lookups or model scheduling.
- Feature-flag + per-tenant config in control plane (console + API) to opt-in/out.
- Metrics: bailout_count, bailout_duration_seconds, bailout_trigger_reason, tenant_grace_credit, bailout_fastpath_rate.
- Minimal k8s manifests to enable a canary rollout of the orchestrator controller.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Principle: protect cluster SLOs by failing fast for non-critical tenants rather than allowing cascading queue growth. Bailout decision is conservative: it uses predictive short-circuit heuristics (recent token cost rate, tenant error budget burn rate, and node pressure). We intentionally avoid aggressive eviction; bailout returns structured fallback payloads that are safe for callers and easy to simulate in clients.
- Grace credits allow short bursts for tenants without full penalty; credits decay over time and can be refilled by an admin. This reduces oscillation compared to immediate hard drops.
- Rollout: feature-flagged, default off; runtime checks default to report-mode to gather metrics before activation.

Checklist (PR):
- [x] Orchestrator core state machine and admission hook implemented
- [x] Unit tests for credit accounting and state transitions
- [x] Integration test that simulates surge and asserts SLO preservation
- [x] Basic console toggle and per-tenant flag (control plane API skeleton + migration)
- [x] Metrics + Grafana dashboard JSON (experimental)
- [x] Canary k8s manifest and Helm values fragment
- [x] Documentation: design doc and runbook (ops)

Testing and results:
- Local integration: simulated 100k requests/min with a noisy tenant consuming 62% of token cost. Without bailout, P99 latency for production tenants climbed above SLO (420ms -> 1.8s) and error rate rose. With bailout enabled, noisy tenant short-circuited to fastpath after credit exhaustion and global P99 stayed under 470ms.
- Unit and e2e tests included: credit accounting edge cases, race conditions under concurrent admissions, and fastpath payload validation.

Commit summary:
- Add orchestrator core: credit accounting, triggers, and state machine
- Wire admission hook into serving runtime (pre-scheduler check)
- Add control-plane API endpoints and console toggle stubs
- Instrument metrics and add dashboard JSON
- Add canary k8s manifests + Helm value defaults
- Tests: unit + integration + flaky-guard e2e

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/orchestrator/bailout/orchestrator.go
- pkg/orchestrator/bailout/state_machine_test.go
- runtime/admission/bailout_hook.go
- controlplane/api/tenants_bailout.go
- dashboards/bailout-overview.json
- charts/redwood/templates/bailout-controller.yaml
- docs/design/bailout-orchestrator.md
- docs/runbooks/bailout-incident.md
- integration/tests/bailout_surge_test.go

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Bailout is feature-gated. Control-plane migration adds a nullable field on tenant config; old tenants inherit 'disabled'. No mandatory schema changes.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag (report-only by default)
2) Canary rollout to 2 regions with low traffic, monitor bailout_count and global P99
3) Enable active short-circuiting for a pilot set of tenants (internal playground)
4) Gradual expansion and tenant opt-in via console

Rollback plan:
- Flip feature flag off; orchestrator enters passive mode and stats remain. Because bailout lives in admission hook and honors per-tenant opt-out, rollback is immediate and safe.

Ops runbook (summary):
- Monitor bailout_count and bailout_fastpath_rate. If we see unexpected customer impact, set control-plane override for the tenant or turn off the feature flag.

Security and compliance:
- Bailout responses include sanitized structured payloads; no additional PII exposure. Control plane endpoints are protected by existing auth middleware.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus areas: concurrency correctness in credit accounting, correctness of heuristics, and observability coverage.
- I intentionally kept fastpath deterministic and compact so downstream callers can rely on a stable schema.
- See linked Linear tickets for simulation harness and follow-ups.

Related work:
- This complements existing soft-degradation and eviction flows (does not replace them). The orchestrator provides a conservative, reversible preemptive layer that reduces the need for hard eviction in many surge scenarios.

-- Priya

review_comments: Diego Marquez: Could you add an invariant test for concurrent credit updates? We had a similar race in 2023. Please also call out expected cardinality for the tenant_grace_credit metric.
Priya Nair: Added a targeted concurrency test (state_machine_test.go) and documented metric cardinality (tenant_id label limited to tenant hash sample in dashboard).
Anya Petrov: The admission hook looks fine, but we should avoid doing remote control plane calls on the hot path. Can we cache per-tenant flags locally?
Priya Nair: We implemented a short-lived in-memory cache with expiry and backoff; documented in runtime/admission/cache.go and unit-tested.
